# LS-12 Sanitary Lift Station: Control Narrative (Draft Rev A)

Your input has gaps that the integrator cannot program around. I filled them with proposals marked **Proposed** in Attachment A and listed each one in Section 10. The most important are:

1. **Lag stop level and lag speed are not defined.** I propose these as SP-04 and FR-LS12-103.
2. **Only 0.2 m separates LSHH-121 from overflow.** In float control, the station starts pumping at LSHH-121. This leaves little time to recover before discharge to the creek (OI-04).
3. **If the PLC fails, the pumps stop.** A hardwired float backup that runs without the PLC is the only protection against overflow in that case. That backup is not designed yet (OI-05).
4. **The 45 Hz minimum speed has not been checked against static head.** If the pump cannot lift flow at that speed, it will run without pumping (OI-03).

---

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Document | LS-12 Control Narrative, doc no. TBD (OI-19) |
| Module | LS-12 Wet Well and Pumps P-121 / P-122 |

**Conventions**
- All levels, speeds, timers and limits are in Attachment A. The prose refers to them by ID only.
- All levels share one datum, the LIT-121 zero (OI-08).
- "Auto pump" means a pump with its HOA in AUTO.
- "Available" is defined in Section 3.2.
- Test methods:
  - **S** = FAT with simulated I/O
  - **I** = FAT by inspection of configuration
  - **D** = SAT by demonstration on live equipment

---

## 1. Purpose and boundaries

LS-12 collects sanitary sewage in the wet well and pumps it into the force main. The PLC controls wet well level with two VFD-driven submersible pumps. Each pump is sized for full station flow.

| Interface | Boundary |
|---|---|
| Upstream | Gravity sewer inflow to the wet well. The station does not control inflow. |
| Downstream | Force main from the P-121/P-122 discharge header. The station has no discharge instruments. |
| Overflow | Overflow discharges to the creek at elevation D-04. **This is a permit violation.** The primary control objective is to prevent it. |
| Power | Utility supply through the automatic transfer switch (ATS) to the MCC. The standby generator is the emergency source. The ATS transfers on its own logic. The PLC only monitors it. |
| SCADA | Central SCADA over licensed radio. The station must run fully without SCADA. |
| Local | One HOA selector per pump at the MCC. |

**Out of scope:** VFD internal motor protection settings, ATS transfer logic, generator controls, and SCADA historian design.

## 2. Equipment and tags

The LS-12 instrument index is the source for ranges, signal types, and wiring. This table gives the function of each tag in this narrative only.

| Tag | Function in this narrative |
|---|---|
| LIT-121 | Primary wet well level. Used for all normal control. |
| LSL-121 | Low-level float. Pump protection stop (C&E) and pump-down end in float control. |
| LSHH-121 | High-high level float. Backup start (C&E and float control) and level disagreement check. |
| P-121, P-122 | Submersible pumps. |
| VFD for P-121, VFD for P-122 | Speed control and fault/ready/run status. Tags TBD (OI-13). |
| HOA for P-121, HOA for P-122 | MCC selectors. The AUTO position goes to the PLC. Tags TBD (OI-13). |
| ATS | Normal/emergency position and source-available status. Tags TBD (OI-13). |
| Standby generator | Running and common fault status. Tags TBD (OI-13). |
| MCC power monitor | Power good / power fail. Tag TBD (OI-13). |
| PLC radio link | Heartbeat with SCADA. |

---

## 3. States and transitions

The station uses state-based control. Pumps use state-based control with sequence-based start and stop actions (Section 5).

### 3.1 Station states

**Table 3-1: Station states**

| State | Description | Entry permissive | Pump control in this state | Automation level |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| ST-0 Initialize | PLC start-up. The PLC reads inputs and retentive data. | None (forced on PLC start) | All run commands off | Automatic |
| ST-1 Level Control | Normal operation on LIT-121. | LIT-121 good | SEQ-C (Table 5-3) | Automatic |
| ST-2 Float Control | Backup operation on LSHH-121 and LSL-121. | None (forced on LIT-121 bad) | SEQ-D (Table 5-4) | Automatic. The return to ST-1 is operator-prompted. |
| ST-3 Power Fail | MCC power lost. | None (forced on power fail) | All run commands off. The PLC resets pump start timers. | Automatic |

**Table 3-2: Allowed station transitions.** All other transitions are forbidden.

| ID | From | To | Condition | Initiator |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TR-01 | Any | ST-0 | PLC start-up | Auto |
| TR-02 | ST-0 | ST-1 | T-15 expired, power good, and LIT-121 good | Auto |
| TR-03 | ST-0 | ST-2 | T-15 expired, power good, and LIT-121 bad | Auto |
| TR-04 | ST-0, ST-1, ST-2 | ST-3 | Power fail continuous for T-13 | Auto |
| TR-05 | ST-1 | ST-2 | LIT-121 bad (FR-LS12-301, -302) | Auto |
| TR-06 | ST-2 | ST-1 | LIT-121 good continuous for T-16, **and** operator pushes CONFIRM | Operator-prompted |
| TR-07 | ST-3 | ST-1 | Power good continuous for T-06, and LIT-121 good | Auto |
| TR-08 | ST-3 | ST-2 | Power good continuous for T-06, and LIT-121 bad | Auto |

### 3.2 Pump states (one instance each for P-121 and P-122)

**Table 3-3: Pump states.** A pump is **available** only in PS-1.

| State | Description | Entry condition | Allowed exits |
|---|---|---|---|
| PS-0 Not in Auto | HOA in HAND or OFF. The PLC monitors only and sends no commands. | HOA not in AUTO (overrides all states except PS-5) | PS-1 when HOA is in AUTO |
| PS-1 Ready | Available for PLC start. | HOA in AUTO, VFD ready, no latched fault, in service, T-08 expired | PS-2, PS-0, PS-5, PS-6 |
| PS-2 Starting | SEQ-A in progress. | Start request from SEQ-C or SEQ-D | PS-3, PS-5, PS-0 |
| PS-3 Running | Run feedback present. | SEQ-A complete | PS-4, PS-5, PS-0 |
| PS-4 Stopping | SEQ-B in progress. | Stop request | PS-1, PS-5 |
| PS-5 Failed | Latched fault: fail-to-start, fail-to-stop, VFD fault, or motor protection (OI-09). | Any fault cause | PS-1 on operator RESET with cause cleared (operator-prompted) |
| PS-6 Out of Service | Removed from Auto by SCADA command. | Operator OUT OF SERVICE command | PS-1 on operator IN SERVICE command |

### 3.3 State requirements

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-001 | On PLC start-up, the PLC must enter ST-0 and remove all pump run commands. | S: Cycle PLC power with LIT-121 above SP-02. Verify ST-0 and no run command until T-15 expires. |
| FR-LS12-002 | The PLC must change station state only by the transitions in Table 3-2. | S: Force each condition in every state. Verify that only listed transitions occur. |
| FR-LS12-003 | The PLC must change pump state only by the exits in Table 3-3. | S: Force each entry condition in every pump state. Verify the result. |
| FR-LS12-004 | The PLC must keep the lead pump designation through PLC restart and power loss. | S: Note the lead pump. Cycle PLC power. Verify the same lead pump. |
| FR-LS12-005 | The PLC must keep latched pump faults (PS-5) through PLC restart and power loss. | S: Latch a fail-to-start. Cycle PLC power. Verify PS-5. |
| FR-LS12-006 | The PLC must not command a pump in PS-0, PS-5 or PS-6. | S: Put each pump in each state, raise level above SP-03, and verify no command. |

---

## 4. Regulatory control

**Loop: wet well level to pump speed.** This loop is a characterized open-loop function, not PID.

- **PV:** LIT-121, filtered with time constant L-08.
- **Output:** speed reference to the VFD of each running Auto pump.
- **Action:** direct. Speed increases as level increases.
- **Tuning:** none. The VFD acceleration and deceleration ramps are VFD parameters. They are set in the software design spec.
- **HAND mode:** the VFD keypad sets the speed in HAND. The PLC has no control in HAND. This narrative does not specify an operator manual-speed mode from SCADA (OI-20).

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-101 | With one Auto pump running in ST-1, the PLC must set its speed reference to: SP-06 when LIT-121 ≤ SP-02; SP-06 + (SP-07 − SP-06) × (LIT-121 − SP-02) / (SP-03 − SP-02) when SP-02 < LIT-121 < SP-03; SP-07 when LIT-121 ≥ SP-03. | S: Hold LIT-121 at SP-01+, SP-02, the midpoint of SP-02 and SP-03, SP-03, and SP-03+. Verify speed within tolerance L-09 at each point, for rising and falling level. |
| FR-LS12-102 | The speed function must use the same calculation for rising and falling level. | S: Part of the FR-LS12-101 test. |
| FR-LS12-103 | While two Auto pumps run in ST-1, the PLC must command both pumps to SP-07. **Proposed (OI-02).** | S: Raise level to start the lag pump. Verify both at SP-07. Lower level below SP-03 while the lag runs. Verify both stay at SP-07. |
| FR-LS12-104 | In ST-2, the PLC must command every running Auto pump to SP-07. | S: Enter ST-2 and trip LSHH-121. Verify SP-07. |
| FR-LS12-105 | The PLC must apply filter L-08 to LIT-121 for control. Alarms and the bad-PV check must use the unfiltered value. | I: Inspect the configuration. S: Step LIT-121 and verify the filtered response. |

---

## 5. Sequences

### SEQ-A Pump start (per pump; called by SEQ-C and SEQ-D)

**Table 5-1**

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| A1 | Check that the pump is in PS-1. | Pump in PS-1 | 0 s (immediate check) | Abort SEQ-A. Report "not available" to the caller. The caller selects the other pump. |
| A2 | Check stagger: no other pump start within the last T-07. | T-07 expired since the last start of any pump | T-07 | Wait. This is a hold step, not a failure. |
| A3 | Send the speed reference, then set the run command. Pump to PS-2. | VFD run feedback true | T-01 | Remove the run command. Latch fail-to-start. Pump to PS-5. Report "failed" to the caller. |
| A4 | Pump to PS-3. | Complete | None | None |

### SEQ-B Pump stop

**Table 5-2**

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| B1 | Remove the run command. Pump to PS-4. | VFD run feedback false | T-02 | Keep the run command off. Latch fail-to-stop. Pump to PS-5. |
| B2 | Start T-08 for this pump. Pump to PS-1 when T-08 expires. | Complete | None | None |

### SEQ-C Level control cycle (active in ST-1 only)

**Table 5-3**

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C1 Idle | All Auto pumps off. | LIT-121 ≥ SP-02 continuous for T-04, then go to C2 | None. This is a wait state. The high-level alarm (Section 7) covers a failure to start. | None |
| C2 Start lead | Run SEQ-A on the lead pump. | Lead in PS-3, then go to C3 | T-01 (in SEQ-A) | Make the other pump lead. Run SEQ-A on it. If no pump is available, raise "No pump available". Repeat C2 when a pump enters PS-1. |
| C3 Lead running | Speed per FR-LS12-101. | (a) LIT-121 ≤ SP-01 continuous for T-05: go to C5. (b) LIT-121 ≥ SP-03 continuous for T-03: go to C4. | T-09 continuous run | Raise "Excessive run time". Continue running. |
| C4 Lag running | Run SEQ-A on the lag pump. Speed per FR-LS12-103. | (a) LIT-121 ≤ SP-04 continuous for T-05: run SEQ-B on the lag, go to C3. (b) LIT-121 ≤ SP-01 continuous for T-05: go to C5. | T-01 (in SEQ-A) | If the lag fails or is not available, raise "Lag not available". The lead continues in C3 at SP-07. |
| C5 Stop | Run SEQ-B on all running Auto pumps. Make the other pump lead (FR-LS12-204). | All Auto pumps in PS-1 or PS-5, then go to C1 | T-02 (in SEQ-B) | Per SEQ-B |

### SEQ-D Float control cycle (active in ST-2 only)

**Table 5-4**

| Step | Action | Transition condition | Timeout | Failure response |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 Idle | All Auto pumps off. | LSHH-121 active, then go to D2 | None. This is a wait state. The LSHH-121 alarm and the hardwired backup cover this step. | None |
| D2 Start lead | Run SEQ-A on the lead pump at SP-07. | Lead in PS-3, then go to D3 | T-01 (in SEQ-A) | Make the other pump lead and run SEQ-A on it. If no pump is available, raise "No pump available". |
| D3 Pump down | Lead runs at SP-07. If LSHH-121 is still active after T-12, run SEQ-A on the lag. | LSL-121 active, then go to D4 | T-09 continuous run | Raise "Excessive run time". Continue running. |
| D4 Stop | Run SEQ-B on all running Auto pumps. Make the other pump lead. | All Auto pumps stopped, then go to D1 | T-02 (in SEQ-B) | Per SEQ-B |

### Sequence requirements

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-201 | The PLC must start pumps per Table 5-1. | S: Run each step, including a forced fail-to-start (hold run feedback false). |
| FR-LS12-202 | The PLC must stop pumps per Table 5-2. | S: Run each step, including a forced fail-to-stop (hold run feedback true). |
| FR-LS12-203 | In ST-1, the PLC must control pumps per Table 5-3. | S: Ramp LIT-121 through each transition, rising and falling. |
| FR-LS12-204 | After each C5 or D4 stop, the PLC must make the other pump lead. | S: Run three cycles. Verify the lead order P-121, P-122, P-121 (or the reverse). |
| FR-LS12-205 | If only one pump is available, the PLC must use it as lead in each cycle. | S: Put P-122 in PS-6. Run two cycles. Verify that P-121 is lead both times. |
| FR-LS12-206 | If the lead fails in C3 or C4 and LIT-121 > SP-01, the PLC must make the other pump lead and start it without waiting for SP-02. | S: Trip the lead VFD fault at the midpoint of SP-01 and SP-02. Verify that the other pump starts after T-07. |
| FR-LS12-207 | The PLC must not start two pumps within T-07 of each other in any state. | S: Raise LIT-121 above SP-03 in C1. Verify the gap between starts. Repeat on the ST-3 exit. |
| FR-LS12-208 | The PLC must not restart a pump until T-08 expires after its stop. | S: Stop a pump. Force a start request. Verify the delay. |
| FR-LS12-209 | In ST-2, the PLC must control pumps per Table 5-4. | S: Force LIT-121 bad. Trip and reset the floats through two cycles. |
| FR-LS12-210 | While the ATS is in the EMERGENCY position, the PLC must limit the number of running Auto pumps to L-07. | S: Set ATS to EMERGENCY, raise level above SP-03, and verify the limit. Value per OI-06. |
| FR-LS12-211 | VFD auto-restart and VFD auto-reset of faults must be disabled. The PLC controls all restarts. | I: Inspect the VFD parameter files. D: Cycle MCC power with a pump running. Verify that the restart comes from the PLC after T-06. |

---

## 6. Interlocks and permissives

All interlocks are in the LS-12 C&E chart. This narrative does not restate the logic. The C&E chart must contain the following causes. The sequences above depend on them.

| C&E cause (required) | Narrative dependency |
|---|---|
| LSL-121 active: stop pumps (HAND behavior per OI-11) | SEQ-D end; pump dry-run protection |
| LSHH-121 active: hardwired backup run, independent of the PLC (OI-05) | FR-LS12-314 |
| VFD fault: pump stop | PS-5 entry |
| Pump motor protection (thermal, seal), if supplied (OI-09) | PS-5 entry |

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-212 | The PLC must implement each PLC-executed cause in the C&E chart. | S: Run the C&E test sheet cause by cause. |

**SIS:** This narrative specifies no safety instrumented function. Overflow protection is an environmental consequence. Its classification, and any need for an SRS under IEC 61511, comes from the LOPA (OI-15). If the LOPA assigns a SIF, the SRS governs it. This narrative will then reference it.

## 7. Alarms

The LS-12 rationalized alarm database owns all alarm setpoints, priorities, delays and responses. The PLC must generate the events below so that the database can use them. The values that Operations requested are given in Attachment A.3 to transfer into the database.

LIT-121 bad · Float disagreement · High wet well level (LIT-121) · LSHH-121 active · LSL-121 active · Overflow in progress · P-121/P-122 fail-to-start · fail-to-stop · VFD fault · not in Auto · out of service · No pump available · Lag not available · Excessive run time · Station in float control · MCC power fail · ATS on emergency · Generator fault · SCADA comms fail · PLC UPS alarms (OI-07).

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-213 | The PLC must generate each event in this section. Each event must have a PLC time stamp. | S: Force each cause. Verify the event and time stamp at SCADA. |

---

## 8. Abnormal handling

### 8.1 Bad PV (LIT-121)

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-301 | The PLC must declare LIT-121 bad when the signal is below L-01 or above L-02 continuous for T-10. | S: Inject each limit for T-10 minus 1 s and for T-10. Verify no declaration and then declaration. |
| FR-LS12-302 | The PLC must declare LIT-121 bad when LSHH-121 is active and LIT-121 is below L-03. | S: Hold LIT-121 at the mid-range. Trip LSHH-121. Verify LIT-121 bad and TR-05. |
| FR-LS12-303 | The PLC must raise "Float disagreement" when LSL-121 is active and LIT-121 is above L-04. This event alone must not change the station state. | S: Hold LIT-121 at the mid-range. Trip LSL-121. Verify the alarm and no state change. The C&E stop still applies. |
| FR-LS12-304 | When LIT-121 becomes good in ST-2, the PLC must show the return prompt (Section 9) after T-16. It must stay in ST-2 until the operator pushes CONFIRM. | S: Restore the signal. Verify the prompt timing. Verify that there is no transition without CONFIRM. |

### 8.2 SCADA communications loss

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-305 | The PLC must continue all control in the current state during comms loss. | S: Disconnect the radio. Run one complete SEQ-C cycle. |
| FR-LS12-306 | The PLC and SCADA must each detect a heartbeat loss within T-11. | S: Disconnect the radio. Time the detection at both ends. |
| FR-LS12-307 | The PLC must store all Attachment A operator setpoints as retentive values. SCADA must write a setpoint only on an operator change. SCADA must not write setpoints when comms come back. | S: Change SP-02 locally in the PLC test tool. Disconnect and reconnect the radio. Verify that SP-02 is not overwritten. |
| FR-LS12-308 | The PLC must buffer time-stamped events during comms loss for L-10 and send them when comms come back. | S: Disconnect the radio. Force three events. Reconnect. Verify all three with their original time stamps. |

### 8.3 Power loss and restart

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-309 | On TR-04, the PLC must remove all run commands and reset SEQ-A and SEQ-B timers. It must not latch fail-to-start or fail-to-stop because of the power loss. | S: Force power fail during SEQ-A step A3. Verify no PS-5 latch. |
| FR-LS12-310 | On exit from ST-3, the PLC must start pumps by normal state logic, with the stagger of FR-LS12-207. | S: Hold LIT-121 above SP-03 in ST-3. Restore power. Verify the first start after T-06 and the second start after T-07. |
| FR-LS12-311 | The PLC and the radio must continue to operate through a power transfer (UPS per OI-07). | D: Open the utility breaker. Verify that SCADA shows the ATS transfer and MCC power events without a comms loss. |

### 8.4 Overflow event record (permit support)

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-312 | The PLC must record the start time, end time and duration of each period with LIT-121 ≥ D-04. The record must be kept in the PLC through comms loss. | S: Hold LIT-121 at D-04 for a set time. Verify the record at SCADA after a comms loss and restore. Reporting needs per OI-14. |

### 8.5 Fail positions

**Table 8-1**

| Failure | Required result | Requirement / test |
|---|---|---|
| PLC CPU stop or watchdog | All PLC run outputs off. The hardwired LSHH-121 backup runs the pumps (OI-05). | FR-LS12-314. S/D: Put the CPU in STOP. Trip LSHH-121. Verify that the pumps run and stop per the C&E. |
| VFD loses its speed reference while running | VFD runs at preset L-06 | FR-LS12-313. I: Inspect VFD parameters. S: Open the reference. Verify the preset. |
| VFD loses its run command | VFD stops (coast or ramp per the software design spec) | Part of FR-LS12-202 |
| LIT-121 signal loss | ST-2 | FR-LS12-301 |
| Float wire break | Per the plant fail-safe convention (OI-12) | C&E test |
| Radio loss | Station stays autonomous | FR-LS12-305 |
| Utility loss | ATS transfers. Station goes to ST-3, then restarts. | FR-LS12-309, -310 |

## 9. Operator interface

**SCADA display (FR-LS12-401):** The display must show:
- LIT-121 level with SP-01 to SP-04 marked
- the LSL-121 and LSHH-121 states
- station state (ST-0 to ST-3)
- lead pump
- for each pump: pump state, HOA in AUTO, speed reference and feedback, run hours, and starts in the last hour
- ATS position and generator status
- comms status
- overflow records

Test S: Verify each item against forced values.

**Operator commands (FR-LS12-402):**

| Command | Access level | Allowed in |
|---|---|---|
| Change SP-01 to SP-04, SP-06, SP-07 | Operations supervisor | Any state |
| Pump OUT OF SERVICE / IN SERVICE | Operator | Any state |
| Pump fault RESET | Operator | PS-5 only |
| CONFIRM return to level control | Operator | ST-2 with prompt shown only |

Test S: Try each command at each access level and in each state.

| ID | Requirement | Test |
|---|---|---|
| FR-LS12-403 | The PLC must reject a setpoint entry outside its limits in Attachment A. It must also reject an entry that breaks the order D-02 < SP-01 < SP-02 ≤ SP-04 < SP-03 < D-03. SCADA must show the reason. | S: Enter a value out of order and a value out of range. Verify rejection and the message. |
| FR-LS12-404 | SCADA must show the prompts below as written. | I: Compare the screen text with this table. |

**Local:** HOA at the MCC only. The need for a local HMI at the station is OI-16.
